nodes.content: Design recoverable distributed snapshots for migrating stream operators with reordered messages and concurrent worker failures.
requirements: Recovery preserves a consistent cut and exactly-once outputs after any single worker crash.
Maintain at least 85% of snapshot-disabled throughput without globally pausing processing.

nodes.content: Use asynchronous epoch snapshots with per-channel sequence fences, durable in-flight logs, fenced migration handoffs, and transactional sink commits.
How can per-channel cuts remain consistent when reordered records cross migration handoffs and a worker crashes mid-commit?
Durable contiguous-sequence fences and ownership epochs should preserve consistent cuts and exactly-once sink commits despite reordering and mid-handoff crashes.
Specify contiguous-sequence cuts and durable ownership epochs; crash-inject reordered handoffs, then audit recovered cuts and sink duplicates.
Run HandoffCrash-1k with reordered channels and single-worker crashes at ownership and commit boundaries; audit recovered cuts and sink IDs.
HandoffCrash-1k recovered 1,000/1,000 consistent cuts with zero missing or duplicate sink IDs under reordered single-worker crashes.
Given HandoffCrash-1k’s zero violations, adopt fenced epoch handoffs for correctness; defer deployment until throughput reaches 85% of baseline.
Benchmark asynchronous fenced handoffs on MigStream-16; batch channel-log fsyncs to target 85% baseline throughput, then rerun HandoffCrash-1k.
Implement 5-ms group-commit channel logs with durability-gated acknowledgments; measure MigStream-16 throughput and rerun HandoffCrash-1k.
Snapshot prototype v0.3 bundles 5-ms group-committed channel logs, durability-gated acknowledgments, fenced handoffs, and MigStream-16/HandoffCrash-1k reports.
Unaligned snapshots persisting out-of-order buffers and atomically fenced ownership should preserve cuts and exactly-once commits without waiting for gaps.
Extend prototype v0.3 with unaligned buffer persistence; run HandoffCrash-1k gap crashes, auditing cuts, sink IDs, and MigStream-16 throughput.
HandoffCrash-1k found 6/1,000 inconsistent cuts: unaligned buffer capture omitted pre-handoff in-flight records despite fenced ownership.
Use durable sender outboxes and migration-scoped replay barriers; atomically transfer ownership, then replay sequence-deduplicated records into transactional sinks.
How can recovery identify pre-handoff records missing from the receiver when reordered messages arrive after ownership transfer?
Instrument prototype v0.3 against sender-outbox replay; inject reordered pre-handoff records and owner crashes, comparing missing-sequence detection and sink IDs.
Outbox replay detected six pre-handoff gaps; HandoffCrash-1k showed zero inconsistent cuts and zero duplicate sink IDs.
Sender frontiers and receiver bitmaps should expose pre-handoff gaps, enabling replay with consistent cuts and duplicate-free sink commits.
Crash-inject 10,000 reordered handoffs; compare sender frontiers with receiver bitmaps, auditing replayed gaps, recovered cuts, and sink IDs.
GapReplay-10k recovered 10,000/10,000 consistent cuts; frontier–bitmap comparison replayed every missing record with zero duplicate sink IDs.
Integrate sender outboxes and frontier–bitmap replay into prototype v0.3; benchmark MigStream-16 throughput against snapshot-disabled baseline and audit crash-recovered cuts.
MigStream-16 delivered 82% baseline throughput; 4/2,000 crash recoveries found bitmap gaps with pruned outbox entries, producing inconsistent cuts.
Which durable acknowledgment safely gates outbox pruning while raising MigStream-16 throughput from 82% to at least 85% of baseline?
Prune outboxes only after durable checkpoint acknowledgment of receiver bitmaps and committed sink epochs; batch acknowledgments for ≥85% throughput.
Modify prototype v0.3 to batch checkpoint-durable bitmap/sink-epoch acknowledgments before outbox pruning; compare GapReplay-10k cuts and MigStream-16 throughput.
With durable acknowledgment gating, GapReplay-10k recovered 10,000/10,000 consistent cuts and zero duplicate sink IDs; MigStream-16 reached 87% baseline throughput.
Fault-inject checkpoint acknowledgment and outbox GC in modified prototype v0.3; audit single-crash cuts, sink IDs, and MigStream-16 throughput.
GC-fault runs found 3/2,000 inconsistent cuts: durable bitmap acknowledgments triggered pruning before checkpoint-manifest publication, losing fallback replay records.
Patch prototype v0.3 to prune only after published manifests reference durable bitmaps and sink epochs; rerun GC-fault and MigStream-16.
Manifest-gated GC recovered 2,000/2,000 consistent cuts with zero duplicate sink IDs; MigStream-16 sustained 86% baseline throughput.
How should overlapping migrations retain outbox records if a worker crash forces recovery from an older published checkpoint?
Pin outbox ranges per recoverable manifest and migration epoch, then crash-test overlapping handoffs with older-checkpoint fallback and MigStream-16 throughput.
Implement manifest-scoped outbox pins and publication-gated GC; crash-test overlapping handoffs with older-checkpoint fallback, auditing cuts, duplicates, and MigStream-16 throughput.
Snapshot prototype v0.4 adds manifest-scoped outbox pins, publication-gated GC, and older-checkpoint fallback tests for overlapping handoffs.
Shadow-migrate via replicated input logs and received-sequence bitmaps; atomically fence ownership and sink epochs before switching replicas.
Can shadow migration safely fence outputs when delayed records reach the old owner after the replica switches ownership?
Replicated log offsets and sink-epoch fencing should make late old-owner records replayable without duplicate outputs after a shadow switch.
Extend prototype v0.4 with shadow replicas; inject delayed old-owner records and crashes, auditing replicated offsets, cuts, and sink duplicates.
ShadowSwitch-2k found 5 inconsistent cuts: late old-owner records arrived after replica log truncation, defeating offset replay despite sink fencing.
Pin sender outboxes and replica logs until published checkpoint bitmaps cover pre-switch frontiers; replay gaps under fenced sink epochs.
Extend prototype v0.4 to pin replica logs and outboxes until published bitmaps cover pre-switch frontiers; rerun ShadowSwitch-2k.
ShadowSwitch-2k recovered 2,000/2,000 consistent cuts after log pinning, with zero duplicate sink IDs under late-record crashes.
Use barrier-aligned per-key snapshots with migration leases and deduplicated sink transactions; pause only migrating keys, never all workers.
Can per-key barriers cover reordered in-flight records during lease transfer without stalling hot keys below 85% baseline throughput?
Prototype key-local barrier alignment with sequence watermarks; crash-test lease transfers and measure hot-key throughput on MigStream-16.
Using v0.4 and ShadowSwitch-2k’s pinned-log baseline, crash-test reordered lease transfers; compare key-barrier cuts, sink duplicates, and MigStream-16 hot-key throughput.
KeyBarrier-2k recovered 2,000/2,000 consistent cuts with zero missing or duplicate sink IDs; MigStream-16 hot-key throughput reached 86% baseline.
Adopt key-local barriers for migrating hot keys: KeyBarrier-2k preserved every cut and reached 86% baseline throughput.
Integrate key-local barriers with v0.4 pinned replay and fenced sinks; crash-test reordered handoffs, audit cuts, and verify ≥85% MigStream-16 throughput.
Add key-local barriers to prototype v0.4; run KeyBarrier-10k crash/reordering trials and MigStream-16 throughput with pinned replay and fenced sinks.
Snapshot prototype v0.5 integrates key-local barriers, manifest-pinned replay, fenced sink epochs, and KeyBarrier-10k/MigStream-16 test reports.
